column1: # deep32-wizard-errors.tsv: what the setup wizard says when a step fails.
# Both wizards (bash and PowerShell) read this one file. Lines starting with # are comments; blank lines
# are ignored. Every row has six fields separated by one TAB:
#   kind     exit (key TOOL:STATUS), code (a code a tool prints, found as a whole word in a line) or
#            text (a regular expression tried against one output line; rows are tried top to bottom)
#   key      as above; text keys use only the regex subset bash and .NET read alike
#   os       any, linux, windows or macos; the wizard uses its own OS row, else the any row
#   source   the tool that prints it: setup, get, inventory, forge, connect, relay, docker, tailscale or
#            wizard (the Workstation VM guide's own checks, and Send disc 2)
#   meaning  what happened, in one or two short sentences
#   fix      at most five steps separated by " | ", each saying where to do it
# The last text row (key ".") catches every line no other row explains.
# tests/wizard/test_error_table.py checks this file against the scripts' own messages and exit statuses.
